About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Embedded partnerships put Ramp inside the software our customers already use to run their businesses. Partners host the Ramp application, manage budgets and limits in their own UI, and trigger payments inside their own workflows. Our first partners are live or launching now, and the job from here is to activate their customers at scale.

As our first Embedded Partner Account Manager, you'll own our signed partners from signature onward and carry their activation number. ISV Account Executives sign new partners and hand them to you with a 24-month activation forecast you've co-signed. From there, you run the relationship, the activation plan, and the joint go-to-market.

You'll work with our Technical Partner Manager, Partner Consulting, Growth, Sales, and CX. They own integration design, bank approvals, customer onboarding, and technical support, so your time goes to activation. Most customers will activate inside the partner's product without talking to Ramp, so you'll make that funnel convert and work the accounts that get stuck.

What You'll Do

  • Agree on the number, then own the partner - co-sign the 24-month activation forecast before signature, take the handoff from the ISV AE, and run the kickoff with our Technical Partner Manager. From there, you're the partner's day-to-day and executive contact.

  • Run the partner cadence - weekly during launch, monthly once live, and a quarterly business review on activation vs forecast. Keep one joint action plan with a Ramp owner, a partner owner and a date on every row, and escalate when dates slip.

  • Own each partner's activation plan - based on the motion (product-led, sales-led, or migration) and set funnel targets from the forecast model. Build the joint marketing calendar with Growth, from co-branded campaigns and webinars to event follow-up. Audit every place Ramp shows up in the partner's product, and get the customer lists and account mapping our campaigns need.

  • Enable both sales teams - run seller kickoffs and keep battlecards, FAQs, and pricing guidance up to date in the partner's sales hub. Give our AEs a partner demo account and the integration story. Make sure every rep on both sides knows the customer offer and their incentive.

  • Run joint selling and work the exceptions - review shared pipeline with the partner's sales team weekly, and pair Ramp and partner reps on strategic accounts. Keep one deal channel where our AEs and theirs coordinate every shared deal. Work stuck applications, approved-but-not-onboarded accounts, and priority customers, routing sales-led deals to Ramp AEs and self-serve wins to CS.

  • Report the number every week - activated customers and contribution profit vs forecast, by partner and by motion. Show where the funnel stalls between lead and activation, with the blocker and its owner. Keep attribution clean so partner credit and rev share are right.

  • Grow the partnership - own amendments, renewals, and new products inside each agreement, including rev share and attribution terms. Bring in Partner Consulting for any new build.

  • Write the playbook - turn what works with our first partners into the activation kit, enablement and launch checklist every new partner starts with. Automate repetitive work so each new partner takes less of your time.

What You Need

  • 4+ years in account management, partner management, customer success or B2B sales.

  • You've grown a book you inherited, not just closed new logos - adoption, activation or expansion against a quota.

  • Fluency with funnels and data. You can read a cohort, find where customers stall, and pull your own numbers from Salesforce and dashboards.

  • You can run a relationship with a partner's executives and their product, sales, and marketing leads simultaneously, and hold both sides to their dates.

  • Comfort with APIs and integrated products. You don't write code, but you can walk a customer's path through a partner's product and tell a product gap from a process gap.

  • Clear, structured writing. Your weekly update tells a partner exec what moved, what's stuck and what you need from them.

  • You've carried a number while building the process around it. The playbooks, dashboards and handoffs for this motion are still being written, and you'll write a lot of them.

  • You use AI every day to research accounts, build reports and draft enablement.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience in embedded finance, payments, card programs or fintech partnerships

  • Experience managing ISV, platform or channel partners

  • Experience growing a self-serve funnel inside a partner's product, such as in-product placements, marketplace listings or partner-hosted sign-up

  • Experience enabling a partner's sales team or launching a product through a partner

  • Experience negotiating amendments, rev share or partner incentives

  • Familiarity with Salesforce, Crossbeam and Gong

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? Coinbase is building the future of finance for people, institutions and their agents, with one place to trade crypto, equities, derivatives and prediction markets, use stablecoins, and connect AI agents with clear controls. The bar is high and the pace is intense, and we like it that way. This isn’t a place for complacency. It’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits and do the best work of your career. If you’re ready to build the future of finance with a championship team who refuse to settle for “good enough,” you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for in-person working sessions

Coinbase Canada is seeking a Head of Finance, Canada to lead the financial and regulatory reporting function for our Canadian regulated business. Reporting to the Director of Reporting and Technical Policy within the Accounting organization, you will serve as the enterprise Finance authority for Canadian reporting, regulatory capital, and OSC and CIRO submissions.

This strategic leadership role defines the target-state operating model, sets scalable reporting and control standards, and represents Finance with senior leaders, the Board, the OSC, and CIRO. The role requires direct ownership of both Form 31-103F1 and CIRO Form 1, from data sourcing through review, submission, and remediation.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the strategy, governance, and process architecture for Coinbase Canada’s financial and regulatory reporting function.
  • Lead audit-ready preparation of Form 31-103F1, CIRO Form 1, and applicable OSC and CIRO submissions.
  • Set standards for IFRS books, parallel ledgers, reconciliations, capital calculations, and supporting documentation.
  • Represent Finance in OSC and CIRO examinations, inquiries, meetings, filings, and remediation matters.
  • Advise executives and the Board on financial performance, regulatory capital, liquidity, control health, and emerging risks.
  • Partner across Tax, Treasury, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Product, and Technology to align reporting, capital, liquidity, and strategy.
  • Build organizational capability through talent development, succession planning, outsourced-provider governance, and KPI/SLA accountability.
  • Drive responsible automation and AI adoption that improves reporting quality, efficiency, control effectiveness, and auditability.

Required Skills and Experience

  • 13+ years of progressive finance, accounting, or regulatory reporting experience within a Canadian investment dealer, securities dealer, bank, fintech, regulator, or professional services firm.
  • Successfully passed the Chief Financial Officer Qualifying Examination and the Partners, Directors and Officers Qualifying Examination, each administered by the Canadian Securities Institute (CSI) and the Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO).
  • 5+ years of direct ownership and preparation of both CIRO Form 1 and Form 31-103F1 for a Canadian regulated entity.
  • Direct experience managing the filing lifecycle, including calculations, accounting judgments, review and sign-off, submission, regulator follow-up, and remediation.
  • Experience in a self-clearing or introducing broker-dealer environment, with expertise in dealer capital adequacy, regulatory capital, liquidity, and related controls.
  • CPA or equivalent accounting designation required.
  • Expert knowledge of IFRS, NI 31-103, Form 31-103F1, CIRO capital adequacy, and Canadian securities-regulatory reporting.
  • Demonstrated enterprise-level leadership, regulator-facing judgment, executive communication, and Board influence.
  • Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

Circle (NYSE: CRCL) is one of the world’s leading internet financial platform companies, building the foundation of a more open, global economy through digital assets, payment applications, and programmable blockchain infrastructure. Circle’s platform includes the world’s largest regulated stablecoin network anchored by USDC, Circle Payments Network for global money movement, and Arc, an enterprise-grade blockchain designed to become the Economic OS for the internet. Enterprises, financial institutions, and developers use Circle to power trusted, internet-scale financial innovation. Learn more at circle.com.

What you’ll be part of:

Circle is committed to visibility and stability in everything we do. As we grow as an organization, we're expanding into some of the world's strongest jurisdictions. Speed and efficiency are motivators for our success and our employees live by our company values: High Integrity, Future Forward, Multistakeholder, Mindful, and Driven by Excellence. We have built a flexible work environment where new ideas are encouraged and everyone is a stakeholder.

What you’ll be responsible for

As a Principal Product Manager on Circle’s Platform team, you will shape the shared services that every Circle product is built on. The Platform team builds the reusable foundation behind Circle’s stablecoin, payments, custody, and developer products — the capabilities that let product teams ship faster, give customers a consistent enterprise-grade experience, and let Circle scale without rebuilding the same infrastructure in every product.


You will identify where shared capabilities – identity & access management, enterprise controls and policy, wallets infrastructure, developer tooling, and the foundations for AI agents – create the most leverage, define strategy and roadmaps that balance consistency with flexibility, and drive adoption across product teams. You will also help define how Circle’s platform serves a world where AI agents are first-class users — with the identity, scoped permissions, controls, and auditability that make autonomous activity safe.


What you’ll work on

  • Define and own product strategy and multi-year roadmaps for core Platform services, connecting company priorities, product team needs, and customer outcomes into a clear point of view on what to build, what to standardize, and what to leave to product teams.
  • Define how the platform supports AI agents and agentic workflows, including agent identity, scoped and delegated permissions, spend and policy controls, human-in-the-loop approvals, and auditable automated actions.
  • Make Circle’s platform agent-ready by design, so agents can discover, understand, and reliably use Circle products through well-structured APIs, MCP servers, tool definitions, and machine-readable documentation.
  • Build shared, self-serve platform capabilities that product teams can adopt with minimal custom engineering — with clear APIs, configuration, documentation, and service boundaries.
  • Lead customer and internal discovery with enterprises, developers, and Circle product teams to understand needs, validate solutions, and turn feedback into roadmap priorities.
  • Drive cross-product adoption and migration onto shared services, sequencing work so existing customers and products move with minimal disruption.
  • Partner deeply with engineering, design, security, compliance, legal, risk, finance, operations, and commercial teams to translate technical, regulatory, and business requirements into clear product requirements and executable plans.
  • Represent Platform priorities in senior product, engineering, and business forums, influencing tradeoffs across speed, security, reliability, customer experience, cost, and long-term leverage.
  • Contribute to platform domains such as wallets and key management, billing and monetization, reporting and data access, and developer settings, bringing a consistent model across products while supporting product-specific needs.
  • Define and report on platform success metrics, such as adoption by product teams, time to launch new products, reliability, operational efficiency, developer experience, and customer satisfaction.
  • Shape the enterprise foundation of Circle’s products, including organizations and workspaces, identity and authentication, roles and permissions, approval policies, audit logging, and the controls enterprise and institutional customers expect.

What you’ll bring to Circle

  • 10+ years of product management experience, including substantial experience building platform, infrastructure, developer, or enterprise products at a cloud, payments, fintech, or B2B SaaS company.
  • Breadth and domain expertise across core platform areas: such as identity and access management, multi-tenant account and organization models, authorization and policy, audit, data and reporting, and developer APIs.
  • Fluency in AI and agentic systems, and hands-on experience using AI tools for product discovery, prototyping, technical research, and workflow automation.
  • Strong technical fluency with distributed systems and platform architecture, including APIs and SDKs, event-driven systems, data models, service boundaries, reliability, and security, with the ability to reason through tradeoffs alongside engineers and architects.
  • Experience building enterprise administration and controls, such as SSO, RBAC, approval workflows, audit logs, or customer-facing reporting.
  • Proven ability to define strategy for horizontal platforms that serve many internal and external customers, and to turn ambiguous, cross-team needs into clear priorities, roadmaps, and measurable outcomes.
  • A track record of driving adoption of shared services across multiple product teams, including migrating existing customers and products onto new platforms.
  • Ability to operate across long-term platform strategy and near-term execution, especially in environments with complex dependencies, many internal customers, and competing priorities.
  • Strong business judgment, with the ability to connect platform investments to product velocity, customer adoption, revenue, operational cost, risk posture, and competitive position.
  • Experience partnering with engineering, security, compliance, legal, risk, finance, and commercial teams on products where security, reliability, regulatory readiness, and customer trust are non-negotiable.
  • Demonstrated leadership influencing executives and senior cross-functional stakeholders through crisp written narratives, strategic tradeoff analysis, and clear decision framing.
  • Highly analytical and metrics-driven, with experience defining platform health, adoption, and operational KPIs.

Before applying, we encourage you to visit us to learn more:

Website | X/Twitter | LinkedIn

About the role

Securitize is hiring a Social Media Manager to build our brand on social and run it every day. You will own how we show up on X, LinkedIn, Reddit, YouTube, Substack, and others as appropriate, and grow a community around those channels that knows our voice and engages with it.

This is a hands-on role. You will write the posts, answer the replies and decide what we jump on, working very closely with our Creative Director, Events Director and Communications Director. Brand, voice and strategy

  • Build and run the social strategy for Securitize, with a clear role for each channel and goals tied to brand awareness, community growth and business results.

Content

  • Must utilize high-degree of judgement in real time about what to engage with, when, and how.
  • Comfort with analytics: setting KPIs, building simple dashboards and explaining results to senior leaders in plain terms.
  • Working knowledge of social management and listening tools (Sprout Social, Hootsuite, Brandwatch or similar) and of Asana or a similar tool for content and approval workflows.
  • Experience using AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude or similar) in your content workflow.
  • A portfolio you can walk us through, including accounts you have grown and posts that performed.

Nice to have

  • Experience at a crypto exchange, brokerage, asset manager or tokenization company.
  • Experience running social at a public company around earnings and other material announcements.
  • Short-form video skills, including scripting, basic editing and clipping long-form content.
  • Executive social or ghostwriting experience for C-suite leaders.

Become a part of our rapidly expanding organization and enjoy a supportive and rewarding work environment:

We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital or family status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

About Aspora

People on the move deserve a bank that moves with them. Since 2022, Aspora has been building a borderless financial operating system that makes money as mobile and transparent as its users.

Backed by influential venture capitalists like Sequoia Capital, Greylock Partners, Hummingbird Ventures, Y Combinator & Global Founders Capital. We're a team of 150+ across India, the UK, the UAE, EU and the US, working with extreme ownership, radical candour, and an obsession with customer impact.

We celebrate builders who question assumptions, ship fast, and turn regulatory complexity into elegant solutions. If you’re driven to redefine what global banking can be, we’d love to build the future with you.

About the role

Aspora is a high talent density company hiring in a competitive market. The people we want most are rarely looking, and they have good reasons to stay where they are. We want to win them anyway: reach them, understand what would make them move, and make the case for Aspora in a way that fits each person.

This role exists to make that our strength. You’ll own senior engineering hiring end to end, and senior non-engineering hiring as the company needs it. You’re a matchmaker as much as a recruiter: you bring in people who will thrive here, hold the bar alongside hiring managers, and when a funnel stalls, find out why and fix it.

You’ll hire globally, across India, the UK, the UAE and Europe. You’ll work directly with the leaders and executives building the company, in a place where hiring is one of the top priorities. And you’ll own the outcome: this is for someone who has done great work with support around them and is ready to do it their way.

Location: Bangalore || In Office

Who you’ll work with

You report to the Head of People Success and work with key engineering, product and business leaders and executives, alongside the recruiting team in People Success.

What experience we are looking for

  • Closed people who weren’t looking: has hired senior engineers or engineering leaders who were passive, from first message to signed offer.

  • Owned it in-house: has run engineering searches end to end inside a product company or startup.

  • Talked a manager off the unicorn: can name a brief they reshaped with a hiring manager using market evidence, and the hire that followed.

  • Runs on their own funnel numbers: tracks response, pass-through and time in stage, and can show a fix that came from them.

  • Closed inside the band: has closed senior offers while holding internal pay parity, and can explain how.

  • Speaks engineer: can talk about scope, systems and seniority with a senior engineer well enough to qualify and sell.

What matters to us in this role

  • When a candidate says they’re not interested, they find out why, then make the role and Aspora appealing to that person.

  • They act as a matchmaker: they bring in people who will thrive here, and tell a candidate honestly when Aspora isn’t the right place.

  • They help hiring managers get clear on the scope and impact of a role, test unicorn wishlists against the real market, and keep the process about hiring, not rejecting.

  • They close offers without breaking pay parity.

  • When a funnel breaks, they find the real cause and fix it without being chased.

Why Join Aspora

  • Define how Aspora wins talent. The pitch, the outreach and the hiring manager partnerships you build become how we hire for the roles that matter most.

  • Work directly with the people building the company. Founders, executives and the leaders of engineering, product and the business are your partners on every senior hire.

  • Hire for a company growing in four directions at once: new products, new countries, new diaspora and, next, the businesses our customers build.

  • Own global searches end to end from your first week, with a direct line to the people who make the decision.

  • Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and ESOPs aligned with Aspora's long-term vision.

About Us

Established in 2018, Bybit is one of the world’s leading cryptocurrency exchanges and digital financial platforms, serving over 90 million users across more than 200 countries and regions. Powered by world-class technology and a user-first mindset, Bybit delivers a seamless ecosystem across trading, payments, wealth management, custody, institutional services, and Web3 — connecting users to the future of digital finance.
 
Our core values define how we build. We listen, care and improve to create products and experiences that put users first. Backed by a global team of ambitious builders, problem-solvers, and innovators, we foster a high-performance and fast-moving environment where talent is empowered to drive real impact at the global scale. Supported by 24/7 multilingual customer service and a strong commitment to innovation, we are shaping the future of finance through technology, collaboration, and bold execution.
 
Today, Bybit is recognized as one of the most trusted and transparent platforms in the digital asset industry, continuing to expand its global presence while building the infrastructure for the next generation of financial services.

Anti-Money Laundering Officer (AMLO) – MiCAR / Crypto

1. Purpose of the Role

The Anti-Money Laundering Officer ("AMLO") is the designated key function holder responsible for establishing, managing, and continuously improving all policies, systems, and processes to counter the risks of the Company's involvement in money laundering, terrorism financing, bribery, and corruption. The AMLO serves as the central point of contact — both internally and externally — for all matters related to AML/CFT compliance.
This role is established in accordance with the Austrian Financial Market Anti-Money Laundering Act (FM-GwG), MiCAR (Regulation (EU) 2023/1114), the Austrian MiCA-VVG, and the FMA's published governance requirements for obliged entities.

2. Key Responsibilities

2.1 AML/CFT Framework & Compliance

  • Design, implement, and maintain the AML/KYC/CFT compliance framework across all business functions
  • Develop and update AML/CFT policies, procedures, and internal controls
  • Ensure rigorous implementation of the framework across the Company, including outsourced functions
  • Monitor regulatory developments and ensure sustained compliance with Austrian and EU AML/CFT requirements

2.2 Risk Management

  • Conduct and maintain the Company's Money Laundering/Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment
  • Identify and assess ML/TF risks related to customers, geographies, products, services, and technologies
  • Implement enhanced due diligence measures for high-risk scenarios (PEPs, complex structures, high-risk jurisdictions)
  • Ensure that ML/TF risks are considered in the development of new products, the taking-on of new customers, and changes to the business profile

2.3 Monitoring & Detection

  • Oversee behavior and transaction monitoring systems
  • Supervise the implementation and effectiveness of automated monitoring tools and alert management
  • Ensure adequate processes for detecting unusual or suspicious activities

2.4 Reporting

  • Act as the primary liaison with the Austrian Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU, A-FIU at the Federal Ministry of the Interior)
  • File Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) as required — independent of management instruction when exercising this function
  • Report at least quarterly to the Board of Directors on relevant events, findings, and compliance status in a formal report
  • Escalate key/high-risk compliance issues within the governance structure

2.5 Sanctions Compliance

  • Oversee sanctions screening processes and systems
  • Ensure compliance with applicable EU and national sanctions regimes
  • Coordinate with the Sanctions Officer on matters of overlapping responsibility

2.6 Training & Awareness

  • Design, implement, and oversee AML/CFT training programs for all staff
  • Ensure staff in relevant functions receive adequate and regular training
  • Promote awareness of AML/CFT obligations and red flags across the organization

2.7 Outsourcing Oversight

Electrical Power Distribution

Supervise installation of MV/LV electrical distribution systems, including switchgear, transformers, generators, UPS systems, busway/busduct, PDUs, panelboards, and branch circuits to the rack. Ensure installations meet design specifications, manufacturer requirements, and applicable electrical codes.

Electrical Installation & Testing

Oversee cable pulling, routing, terminations, grounding, bonding, labeling, and torque documentation. Coordinate electrical inspections, equipment testing, NETA acceptance testing, and system readiness for energization. Work closely with the Superintendent, HV and Electrical SME to manage power system interfaces and energization sequencing.

Own electrical trade sequencing and manpower coordination across electrical rooms, equipment yards, galleries, and white space. Coordinate with mechanical, plumbing, and controls teams to manage installation interfaces, resolve field conflicts, and maintain schedule. Leverage BIM-supported coordination to identify and resolve clashes before installation.

Commissioning & Energization

Drive completion of electrical installation checklists, equipment inspections, testing documentation, and prerequisites supporting Level 1-3 commissioning. Support commissioning execution through Levels 4-5 with the CXQC Field Manager, ensuring electrical systems are ready for functional testing, integrated systems testing, and turnover.

Enforce electrical safety standards, including NFPA 70E, LOTO, arc flash protection, energized work permits, and safe work practices as systems progressively energize around ongoing construction. Hold electrical trade partners accountable for first-time quality, documented QC, and compliance with project specifications.

Own the electrical three-week look-ahead, daily coordination, manpower planning, and progress reporting. Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented.


The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But international fintechs and banks are left with two unsatisfying options to choose from: Either build on legacy correspondent banks that are slow and unreliable, or interface with middleware providers that neither move nor hold the dollars directly, but instead rely on underlying legacy banks themselves. At Augustus, we collapse the stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.


We are a group of ex-founders, founding employees of unicorns, and people who dropped out of university because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and Etched.


We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.

The Role

As CFO Associate at Augustus, you will report to the CFO and work across the whole finance function of a bank: accounts payable and receivable, budgeting and forecasting, the monthly close and the general ledger, board and committee reporting, investor and regulatory reporting, and the financial audit. Finance at Augustus is built like the rest of the organisation: lean, and running on systems rather than headcount. Legacy banks scale finance with people. We build flows that make the work disappear.

You start by taking over the day-to-day work. Then you rebuild it. Every process you run, you think of ways to improve it - not to execute faster, but to remove the manual step altogether. By month six, the day to day runs hands-off and you own projects with engineering, parts of the close, and reporting.

This is the role for someone who wants to run finance one day and understands that the fastest way there is to see every part of a finance organization from the inside, at the moment it is being built.

Your First Six Months

  • Months 1-2: Take over the day-to-day. Run accounts payable end-to-end: set up new vendors, review the bills our automated workflow creates, resolve missing payment accounts and legal entities, and coach colleagues on their part of the process. Run accounts receivable. Sit inside the monthly close, review every system-generated reconciliation and trace every out-of-balance to its root cause. Learn where the process breaks.

  • Months 3-4: Ship the first wave of improvements. Turn the flows you ran by hand into AI-supported flows. Design the reconciliations that don’t exist yet. Contribute to your first board pack: financial statements, variance analysis and forecast.

  • Months 5-6: Own entire projects. You take a new initiative from a blank page to a running process. The manual work from month one runs hands-off; you handle the judgment calls.

  • After Month 6: Support our growth through financial analysis of new products and geographies, and build straight-through processes to manage the related workflow

Who Will Thrive At Augustus

We believe that throwing smart people with high agency at big problems produces the best outcomes. We’re building a modern correspondent bank, and we win by having a better team. The people who succeed here share the following traits:

  • American Dream: You’d rather shoot for gold than settle for mediocrity. You pick the harder goal and stay optimistic when the odds are against you. If it feels easy, we aimed too low.

  • Live Player: You don’t need permission. You rebuild what’s broken without being asked, challenge how things are done, and move before the perfect moment.

  • Ever to Excel: You can’t accept good enough and you take your work personally. When it matters, you do what it takes and keep raising the bar for yourself and your team.

  • Genuine: You play for the company, not your title or turf. Low ego, low drama, no politics. You say it straight, also upwards and always assume good intent.

This role is for you if:

  • You want to be a CFO one day. You know the fastest way there is not a title but breadth: close, AP, AR, audit, regulatory, budgeting, treasury, investor relations, and board reporting - all within your first year, all inside a bank being built from scratch.

  • You’ve done the work you’d be automating and it bothered you that it was manual.

  • You see AI as a way of working, not a feature. You measure yourself by the manual work you’ve removed, not the hours you’ve put in.

  • You want to build a lean finance function: the controls, the reconciliations, the reporting pack. You draft them, defend them and rewrite them when they break.

This is not for you if:

  • You want to specialize. This is a generalistic role across all finance functions.

  • You measure your impact by the size of your team. Success here looks like the bank multiplying in volume while the finance function stays small.

  • You prefer a mature playbook to a blank page. No close checklist tuned over five years, no ERP consultants on retainer, no team standing by.

  • You’re above the work. Before anything gets automated here, someone has to run AP by hand, review the bills and understand the close completely - including you.

Hard Requirements

  • 2+ years in investment banking, finance or accounting roles - at a bank, fintech, high-growth startup, or in audit.

  • Hands-on accounting fundamentals: you have worked a monthly close, you can read a general ledger, and you can trace a reconciling item to its root cause.

  • You use AI tools in your daily work today and can show the manual work they replaced.

  • Based in New York or Berlin, or willing to relocate.

Pay transparency

Compensation packages at Augustus include base salary, equity, and benefits. New hire offers are made based on a candidate’s experience, expertise and geographic location. The annual US base salary range for this role is 150k - 180k + equity.

What We Offer

  • Career Growth: You will be given more responsibility and pushed to grow faster than ever before.

  • Network: Your peers are brilliant, highly motivated people. These people will be foundational in your future opportunities.

  • Real Participation: Employees are shareholders. You will think and act like an owner.

  • Perks & Benefits: Relocation support, visa support, the latest Apple gear (MacBook + AirPods), lunch benefit, gym benefit, a beautiful office in the heart of the city, 4x on-/offsites per year, and an annual development budget.

Additional to the global benefits above, we offer localized benefits such as comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance and a 401(k) retirement plan for our US team.
